questions.title: Fluid Dynamics 1
questions.question_details: We are given a rectangular shaped container with base Area $A_0$ and initial water level is $h$. The water is leaking out from the bottom of the container through a hole with area $A_1$. Find the time taken for the all water to leak out.
instructions: You will now have {thinkTime} to prepare. After that, you will have up to {recordTime} to record your verbal response and plot the function on the highlighted plot grid to the right. You may also use the white board to show any additional calculations or thoughts.
You can press the 'Record' button below when you're ready.

hints.text: Consider using Bernoulli's equation and the continuity equation to solve this problem.

questions.title: Proof Torricelli's Law
questions.question_details: Starting with Bernoulli's Principle, derive Torricelli's Law for the efflux velocity $v$ of a fluid leaking from a small hole at the bottom of a tank with water height $h$.
instructions: You have {thinkTime} to prepare your derivation and strategy.
During the {recordTime} recording, verbally explain your proof using Bernoulli's equation and show the integration steps on the whiteboard to find the total time $T$.
Ensure you state any assumptions made regarding the hole size $A_1$ relative to $A_0$.

hints.text: Recall Bernoulli's Equation: $P + \frac{1}{2}\rho v^2 + \rho gh = \text{constant}$. For the leak time, use the continuity equation: $A_0 \frac{dh}{dt} = -A_1 v$.
Think about how the rate of change of height depends on the square root of height.

questions.title: Resistors with Two Node Problem
questions.question_details: In the circuit shown, a $1\,\text{V}$ source drives a ladder network of $1\,\Omega$ resistors. The bottom rail is grounded. Calculate the voltage at the node labelled $V_x$ (with respect to ground).
instructions: You have {thinkTime} to plan your approach (pick a method such as nodal analysis or equivalent resistance reduction). You can use the whiteboard to show your work.
During the {recordTime} recording, clearly label node voltages and reference ground.
Show a valid circuit-analysis method (recommended: nodal / KCL at $V_x$ and any additional nodes).
Carry the algebra through to a numerical value for $V_x$, and briefly sanity-check the result (for example, that $0 < V_x < 1\,\text{V}$).

hints.text: Use nodal analysis: write KCL at $V_x$ and at the node(s) to the right. All resistors are $1\,\Omega$, so currents are simply voltage differences divided by resistance.

questions.title: Rocket Momentum
questions.question_details: A rocket starts from rest in deep space. The rocket structure and systems have a mass of $500\,\text{kg}$ and it initially carries $500\,\text{kg}$ of fuel. When the engines are fired, fuel is ejected from the rocket at a constant speed of $100\,\text{m\,s}^{-1}$ relative to the rocket. How fast will the rocket be moving when all the fuel has been used up?
instructions: You have {thinkTime} to plan your solution strategy and identify the key equations.
During the {recordTime} recording, derive the rocket equation using conservation of momentum.
Clearly define the system mass at times $t$ and $t+dt$, and explain the sign convention for the exhaust velocity.
Show the integration steps leading to the final velocity expression $v_f$.

hints.text: Consider an infinitesimal time interval $dt$ and apply conservation of momentum to the combined system of the rocket and the expelled fuel.
